races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Eager Lad
runners_data.note: Debutant for A Oliver (2 wins from 10 runners in past 14 days), unknown style and going on debut, lightly-raced flag applies — raw ability is the complete unknown here and Carroll in the saddle gives no prior lead.|

runners_data.name: Optics
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose two runs came over 6-7f at Goodwood and Headfort, dropping back to 5f here raises a trip query and the form figures of 0-7 offer little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, recorded a 7th at 6f Goodwood and a 10th on the same track, trainer Feane T14 0/5 — limited evidence for optimism but races on going that suits.|

runners_data.name: Beach Barbie
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 5f on Standard Dundalk going, so genuine course-and-distance form is the angle here; however, her true style is hold-up and she is pushed to midfield in this crowded pace map, which will blunt the finishing threat she has shown on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Miss McLoughlin's 4-year-old has run predominantly over 7f at Goodwood and trips beyond her comfort zone, with all five recent runs in the 5th-12th range; genuine hold-up racer redistributed closer to the pace than ideal, making her prospects even harder to envisage.|

runners_data.name: Forbidden
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race, with two poor runs at 6f on good ground behind her, but she receives a significant tactical upgrade by leading uncontested over 5f on Standard — the fades-in-finish flag is the key risk if the leader slows and gets caught.|

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Finished 3rd at 5f Curragh on good and 9th at 6f on soft for J A Stack — the 5f form is encouraging and dropping back in trip suits; Heffernan booked and lightly raced, making this one of the more interesting unknown quantities in the field.|

runners_data.name: Institute
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's prominent-style runner has two placed efforts at 5-6f on this surface and at Goodwood, and Wayne Lordan takes the ride — best-credentialled prominent racer to track Forbidden and the most likely to convert if the leader weakens.|

runners_data.name: McHenry Sunrise
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish flag compounds the redistribution issue — a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield over 5f, and the run record of 8th, 4th, 10th over 5-6f gives little reason to expect improvement from a compromised position.|

runners_data.name: Nebrook Star
runners_data.note: Diego Lima rides this 3-year-old whose best effort is a 3rd at 5f on good ground — the sim-going record shows just 1 run from 6 on comparable surfaces, and the hold-up style looks poorly suited to the pace map here.|

runners_data.name: Off We Go
runners_data.note: Two runs, both double-figure finishes at 6f Curragh on good ground, with fades-in-finish flag and tongue strap headgear noted — nothing in the form to suggest a reversal and the hold-up style is squeezed out by the congested rear.|

runners_data.name: Osterode
runners_data.note: The single run of 4th at 5f Curragh on good going is directly course-distance relevant and McDonogh rides; visor headgear worn first time adds intrigue — lightly-raced flag means upside exists and this is one of the better-credentialled unknowns in the field.|

runners_data.name: Tudor Flame
runners_data.note: Debutant for the same Feane yard that also saddles Strikepoint; unknown going and style with a lightly-raced flag, but Leigh Roche takes the ride and first-time-out runners from this stable carry limited expectation given T14 0/5.|

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Browne McMonagle takes the mount for Grassick, and White Smoke's best effort is a 4th at 5f on good going — the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 signals a meaningful discount, as a genuine hold-up horse racing out of position will struggle to produce her best over this flat 5f trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Forbidden is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 5f maiden and should dictate from the gates, setting a sustainable pace without any serious challenger pressing from the outside — the field behind is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types. Institute is the only genuine prominent racer capable of tracking Forbidden through the early stages, giving the leader a degree of cover rather than real pressure. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Beach Barbie, White Smoke, Famed Again and McHenry Sunrise are all true closers but will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, compromising their natural finishing kick. A sustainable, uncontested lead over 5f on Standard Dundalk turf is a significant tactical advantage, and this race shape strongly favours horses who can either lead or track closely in the first two positions, with genuine hold-up horses squeezed out of their preferred role and unlikely to generate the late burst they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forbidden Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Forbidden leads comfortably without early pressure and Institute tracks closely, allowing the front two to control fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: Forbidden dictates every yard on a flat 5f track with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, conserving energy for the finish; a prominent stalker like Institute or a lightly-raced unknown like Grande Cuvee or Osterode could benefit from the low-pressure pace by sitting within striking range and pouncing late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Sweeps Past
scenarios.trigger: If Forbidden sets a strong but not run-away gallop and a prominent-tracking rival sustains momentum to reel it in late.
scenarios.body: Institute, trained by A P O'Brien with two Dundalk places at 5f and 6f, is ideally placed to track the leader and unleash a finishing effort on this flat track; a lightly-raced unknown such as Eager Lad or Tudor Flame — both debutants with unknown styles — could emerge from the prominent group with unexposed ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Unexposed Talent
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced or debut runners (Eager Lad, Tudor Flame, Osterode) shows superior raw ability that trumps positional disadvantage.
scenarios.body: With three runners carrying UNKNOWN style tags and lightly-raced flags, any one could be making a significant forward move from an unexposed base; Osterode, who ran 4th on debut at 5f at the Curragh in good ground, has direct course-distance form and could outclass this field if that run merely scratched the surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overcome Crowded Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and the redistributed hold-up horses find gaps to deliver their natural finishing runs despite adverse positioning.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands that Beach Barbie, White Smoke or Famed Again — all true hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal — somehow recover their natural style and finish strongly; given their STYLE_FIT discounts and the compressed 5f trip leaving minimal time to make up ground, this remains the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Forbidden in the early strides — if she is allowed to bowl clear unchallenged, her lone front-running role over 5f on Standard going is a significant tactical weapon that the field may simply lack the pace to counter.

Institute is the one prominent-style runner capable of tracking Forbidden throughout; if Wayne Lordan can keep him close to the lead in second or third, he is best-placed of all to capitalise if Forbidden fades inside the final furlong.

Osterode with McDonogh and a visor first-time is the most interesting unexposed runner — a 4th on debut at 5f Curragh is solid form and the headgear change could unlock improvement; watch the market for any significant drift or support.

Beach Barbie, White Smoke and Famed Again will all be forced to race closer than their natural hold-up style demands — if they get competitive early fighting for position, it could create mid-race crowding that disrupts the pack and opens up room for a prominent-tracking rival.

Grande Cuvee for J A Stack (same yard as McHenry Sunrise) had a promising 3rd at 5f Curragh — Seamie Heffernan's booking in a maiden of this nature is worth noting as a possible yard confidence indicator.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden
BAR 1 Betting 'Download Our App' Mourne Handicap

runners_data.name: Sir Les Patterson
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Stephen Thorne with a mixed recent record, finishing 4th on this Standard course last time in similar company — his six-run form string includes too many mid-field finishes (10th, 6th, 14th) to inspire confidence, though the going is fine for him.|
runners_data.comment: Sir Les Patterson brings distance and going experience to this test and steps back up in trip on a workable 28-day break, carrying 145 lb from stall six; the concern is that his recent form has been patchy, with just one win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's 5yo hold-up type who placed 7th last time out in a bumped sequence of double-figure finishes on good ground, suggesting Standard at Dundalk flatters him on paper but his recent form has been poor.|
runners_data.comment: Valiant Force has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a freshener of 34 days, carrying 140 lb from stall 4 with an official mark of 100 to his name; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with a seventh the best of those efforts.

runners_data.name: Black Forza
runners_data.note: Returning from a 90-day absence for trainer M D O'Callaghan with the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle — tongue-tie applied — and although his best runs have been over 5f on Standard, the booking and freshness make him hard to dismiss entirely.|
runners_data.comment: Black Forza shaped with promise when third three starts back, handles today's distance and going, and a rating of 98 puts him firmly in contention from stall seven; the chief concern is that he returns after a 90-day absence yet to score in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who won on Standard over 5f at Dundalk recently, giving him proven course ability, though he steps up to 6f today and is yet to show that extra distance suits; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim helps at the weights.|
runners_data.comment: Kerdos arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving him every reason to go well from stall three carrying 134 lb; our rating of 100 marks him as the one to beat, though his overall recent form does demand some faith.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Recent winner in this grade on Standard going and a lightly-weighted prospect, though his true style is hold-up and with several other closers in the field unable to get their natural position, he will race further forward than ideal, tempering his finishing-kick chance.|
runners_data.comment: Dark Ace brings solid recent placed form — two wins and a pair of thirds in his last six starts — and has experience over today's trip and going, but two unplaced efforts since those placings give pause, and 131 lb is no light burden from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Consistent veteran for Edward Lynam with multiple placed efforts on both Standard and good ground, but his natural hold-up style is compromised by the depth of the field here — Ben Coen takes over in the saddle and will need to find a way through in the straight from further forward than this horse prefers.|
runners_data.comment: Collective Power has shown consistency in recent starts, with a third last time out and a second three starts back, though he remains winless in his last six; the experience over today's trip and going is a plus, but his speed rating of 75 suggests he may struggle to quicken decisively from stall five.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's 5yo has been placed in four of his last six outings and wears a hood (p) — he races prominently and that is genuinely his style here, making him one of the most positionally sound contenders in the race, though his best efforts have come on good ground rather than Standard.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, I Bid You Ajou has hit the frame three times recently but ranks ninth of twelve on our figures, making him hard to fancy at this level; experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after 24 days, offer modest encouragement at best.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Listed as wearing hood (p) and truly a hold-up type, yet pushed into midfield on the map by the congestion of closers at the rear — Patrick McKenna's 6yo ran only six days ago and that quick turnaround is the bigger concern, even if the Standard going is acceptable.|
runners_data.comment: Cuban Grey has shown only one win in his last six starts, with a seventh and fifth sandwiched around it suggesting inconsistency, and he ranks tenth of twelve on our figures; third last time out offers a crumb of comfort, and he does have experience over today's distance and going, but it is hard to make a strong case from stall 12 off 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field for David Marnane, who also saddles Fox In Flight — if Allsortz gets an unchallenged lead at a fair clip over this 6f Standard surface he becomes the controlling force in the race, and his OR of 82 is competitive enough in this grade.|
runners_data.comment: Showed his quality with a win four starts back and was third three starts back, but has disappointed in his last two outings; has run over today's trip and going, and while he carries 119 lb from stall one, those recent efforts leave something to prove.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes over on this 8yo for Ms Claire O'Connell, but the horse is returning from a 376-day absence — an enormous layoff — and his recent Gowran and Dundalk runs produced finishes of 12th, 16th and 18th, so fitness and ability are real questions despite the prominent racing style.|
runners_data.comment: Dandyville arrives here 376 days off the track and winless in his last four starts, which are clear negatives, though he has experience of today's distance and going and a rating of 85 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall two at 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: A 3yo for David Marnane who races in the same stable as Allsortz — in reality a hold-up type pushed forward on the map by the volume of closers in this field; his recent form (8th, 2nd, 9th, 5th, 9th) is inconsistent and he faces a positional compromise today.|
runners_data.comment: Fox In Flight arrives winless in his last six starts and ranks last on our figures, with a speed rating of 74 sitting below his official mark of 79; a second four starts back is the sole encouragement, though ninth last time out and ninth three starts back make him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: All The Girls
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is an asset for T G McCourt's filly, who wears a hood (p) and races prominently — she placed 3rd on Standard at Dundalk over 5f and has been competitive at 6f on good, making her one of the more straightforwardly positioned horses for this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, All The Girls faces a stiff ask here; a third two starts back offers a crumb of hope, and she does have experience of today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Allsortz is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-horse field and should secure an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on Dundalk's standard surface, dictating throughout from the front without meaningful pressure. Behind him, I Bid You Ajou, Dandyville, and All The Girls will look to press for prominent positions, but this is not a strongly pace-pressured race — Allsortz can bowl along at his own rhythm and control the tempo. The field contains a significant cluster of genuine hold-up horses (Dark Ace, Collective Power, Fox In Flight, Cuban Grey) that cannot all settle at the true rear and have been redistributed into midfield, meaning their finishing kicks will be compromised by having to travel further forward than ideal. This race shape strongly favours either Allsortz himself if the pace is truly uncontested and moderate, or horses positioned prominently to track him and pounce, rather than those relying on a late surge from genuine hold-up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Allsortz Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz bowls to the front uncontested and sets a fair but manageable gallop, allowing him to dominate throughout.
scenarios.body: Allsortz gets an untroubled lead and dictates pace to suit himself on this standard Dundalk surface, meaning no horse in behind can build up enough momentum to reel him in over just 6f. Prominent horses I Bid You Ajou and Dandyville may chase but lack the class at the weights to close a controlled gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collars Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz sets an honest pace and the prominent runners tracking him have enough in reserve to overhaul him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: I Bid You Ajou and All The Girls are genuine prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and time their challenge, benefiting from a race where the true hold-up horses are squeezed out of their natural position. Kerdos, who has a recent course win over 5f on Standard and sits off the pace, could also arrive late enough to be involved if the front two tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and one of the closer types can find a clear run to power through.
scenarios.body: Dark Ace has the best recent form figures in this field (ORs of 91 backed by prior wins on Standard) and could benefit if gaps open late, but his redistribution from true hold-up to midfield makes it harder for him to produce a finishing burst from far back. Sir Les Patterson or Valiant Force, sitting off a proper gallop with OK going assessments and decent RPRs, represent the hold-up profile that might land this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes trouble in running, with crowding on the bend hampering the prominent and midfield groups and producing a messy finish.
scenarios.body: With 12 runners on Dundalk's tight track, interference on the turn can scramble the race entirely, and a horse like Kerdos — who has course form and is unexposed here over 6f — could pop up if rivals are shuffled back. Black Forza returns from 90 days off with top jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle booked, offering each-way value if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Dandyville — a 376-day absence is a serious fitness concern and Chris Hayes will need to produce an almost perfect front-to-finish ride for this 8yo who has been showing double-figure placings even when fit.

Fox In Flight and Dark Ace are both true hold-up horses who cannot get their natural position in this 12-runner field — watch for them to be caught in traffic on Dundalk's tight turn and unable to produce their finishing run at the critical stage.

Allsortz is trained by David Marnane who also saddles Fox In Flight — if connections have a preferred runner, watch whether Fox In Flight's jockey (Andrew Slattery) exerts any pace pressure on Allsortz in the early stages that would disrupt the controlled lead scenario.

Black Forza returns from 90 days off with Dylan Browne McMonagle booked — a big-name jockey pick-up on a fresh horse carrying a tongue-tie is a combination worth monitoring in the market before the off.|

runners_data.name: Never Mind Me
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner in the race; Seamie Heffernan booked is significant, but 683 days off the track is a massive flag and the STYLE_FIT flag notes she races out of role — if she rediscovers her best she controls matters, but the layoff makes reliability uncertain.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Recent form shows back-to-back placed efforts including a Dundalk run and good sim-going record (4/15, 1W3P); hold-up type who will need to produce a late effort, though the likely moderate tempo is not ideal for a closer — tp headgear suggests he switches on.
runners_data.comment: Famous Enough has been placed second two of his last three starts and brings distance and going experience, but has been winless in his last six and a rating of 55 leaves him mid-pack in a competitive field of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who fades in the finish, a concern over this mile on a track that exposes stamina limitations; eight-runner sim-going record of 1W2P at the trip is workable but the fade flag reduces confidence at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Roman Harry has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 63 by us against an official mark of 55, he holds a strong case on paper; the concern is his winless recent spell and back-to-back eighth and ninth-placed finishes making it hard to fancy him turning the tables here.

runners_data.name: Movin And Groovin
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this course and distance (1/8f/STA) which is directly relevant; natural hold-up type who will be forced forward from his preferred berth due to the field density — that positional compromise is a real risk despite the obvious form fitness.
runners_data.comment: Movin And Groovin won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but her record in her last five starts reads inconsistently, and 134 lb from stall 14 are the challenges she faces stepping back in.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Won at Dundalk over 7f on Standard and carries light weight for a 3yo; true hold-up horse who will need a clear run in a crowded field, but Dylan Browne McMonagle's course craft gives him every chance of finding a passage if the pace is sufficient.
runners_data.comment: Bullet Bourbon won last time out to arrive here in form, and she has experience of today's trip and going, but 132 lb is a stern burden from stall 17, and her record in recent starts shows she can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Queen Leila
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance and going (1/8f/STA) and has multiple placed efforts at the trip on Standard; hold-up type who has shown she stays and handles the track, though the 114-day absence and the t headgear make it a watch on how fresh she presents.
runners_data.comment: Queen Leila arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while her speed rating of 67 underlines her claims; the chief concern is the 114-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (1d LR) which is an extraordinary fitness flag and must temper any expectation — natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position here; Gavin Cromwell's T14 form is strong (3/22) but the turnaround is extreme.
runners_data.comment: Reponse Finale won two starts back, and finished second last time out, but 129 lb is a hefty burden and just one day's recovery is a significant concern for a filly rated 40 officially.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: One of only three genuinely prominent types in the field alongside the leader; if he presses Never Mind Me he shapes the whole race, but his recent form (867007) and sim-going mark (0W1P) suggest limited upside — tv headgear won't spark a transformation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Rampage arrives here 34 days fresh, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour, though his recent string of unplaced efforts and an official mark of 45 suggest he faces a stiff ask from stall three carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Consistent fader in finishes tagged ⚠, with a poor sim-going record (0W0P in 2 runs); the hold-up style is problematic in a race likely to be run at a modest pace, and being pushed into a midfield position out of role compounds the difficulty further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Tenacious does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, though a return of eighth last time out and little better before that makes it hard to fancy her from stall 7 off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Won last time out (405391, 1/7f/GOO) and arrives in form, but Dundalk Standard is a different surface profile and his sim-going record is 7/15 — the v headgear retained, but as a hold-up horse forced forward in a compressed field he must find more than his OR suggests.
runners_data.comment: Beau Army won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her fair claims, but that ninth two starts back is hard to ignore and she faces 16 rivals from stall one carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Misava
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (80/0-0) and a fade-in-finish flag make her one of the most difficult to back here; pushed into midfield on the map when a true hold-up horse, the h headgear doesn't compensate for form that shows no completion of the course in recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Misava faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 46-day break that could freshen her up.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Won last time out (406521, 1/8f/GOO) and placed over this trip; but that win came on Good ground and sim-going numbers are modest (0W0P) — tp headgear suggests a keenness issue and being a natural hold-up type compressed into midfield is a tactical complication.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Cause I Like You faces a stiff ask, but she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's distance and going; the deeper form — a fifth and sixth in recent starts — makes it difficult to enthuse.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Placed (3/10f/GOO) recently and has course experience, but OR=40 at the bottom of the weights and a true hold-up style forced into a midfield position means he needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to offer; tb headgear retained.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a ninth last time out the most recent evidence, Master Garvey is hard to recommend at a ranking of 14 of 17 on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: One of the three prominent types in the race and therefore tactically relevant, but recent form (096709) is alarming and the fade flag is prominent — if he pushes up to pressure Never Mind Me he shapes the race but is unlikely to be the beneficiary.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last of all on our figures, Six Wings faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and a 32-day break at least means she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: No jockey named which is itself a minor concern; form figures (78698) show consistent mid-division finishes and the fade flag suggests she won't be doing her best work late — t headgear, 44 days off, and poor sim-going make the case hard to construct.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Due In June has run over today's trip and steps back into the contest from draw five carrying 123 lb, but her recent string of mid-to-rear finishes makes improvement hard to envisage after 44 days off.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Fades in finish with a form line showing 09-005; sim-going record is 0W0P and that one placed effort (5/8f/STA) was some time ago — the b headgear is retained but OR=57 at top weight for an in-form rival makes the weight-form combination uncomfortable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Angel Of Promise nevertheless heads the ratings here and her experience over today's trip and conditions gives her every chance from stall 15, with a fifth last time out her best recent effort.

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: Form of 0-0000 is unambiguous; pushed into midfield from a true hold-up position and the fade flag is consistent with the form — t headgear won't reverse a horse who has finished outside the first ten in all recent starts and lacks any sim-going positives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Polanco faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns after a 33-day break with fitness less of a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Never Mind Me is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Rampage and Six Wings as genuine prominent types behind, she faces minimal early pressure and should dictate a controlled, even gallop on Standard Dundalk ground over the mile. With no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, the pace is likely to be honest but not brutal — a tempo set entirely to suit Never Mind Me's rhythm rather than forced by any rival. The real tactical complication is the extraordinary density of hold-up horses in this field: Tenacious, Movin And Groovin, Beau Army, Reponse Finale, Cause I Like You, Master Garvey, Polanco, Due In June, and Misava are all natural closers who cannot all settle at the back of 17 runners — several will be forced wider and closer to the pace than ideal, compressing the midfield and creating a congested bunch through the middle sectors. This race shape — a moderate, controlled gallop set by one unchallenged leader — materially favours horses who can race prominently or travel just off the pace in the first four, rather than true hold-up types who need a strong gallop to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Never Mind Me dictates an uncontested moderate tempo and the pace-compressed midfield struggles to mount a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Never Mind Me settles into a rhythm unchallenged through the early and middle sections, and the lack of a genuine strong gallop means hold-up horses in the congested bunch never get the searching pace they need to reel her in; those racing prominently just behind her are best placed to pounce in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rampage or Six Wings push closer to Never Mind Me early, injecting slightly more pace that eventually softens her but leaves close-up horses best placed.
scenarios.body: A marginally stronger tempo than Scenario A develops through the middle mile, meaning Never Mind Me is reeled in inside the final two furlongs by horses who tracked her off the pace rather than those caught wide in the congested bunch behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow quickens sufficiently in the straight to string the field out and reward the genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A true closer would need an unlikely injection of pace from the front end on a Standard surface, but if Rampage or Six Wings force an honest gallop that burns out Never Mind Me, hold-up horses who find a clear run in a rare-for-this-field strong-tempo shape could arrive late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Congestion Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the overloaded midfield causes significant traffic problems, interference, or checks in the straight that scramble the finish order unpredictably.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners, most of whom are hold-up types compressed into a tight bunch, a wall of horses could block the straight and create gaps that only the widest or luckiest escapee exploits; this is a low-probability but non-trivial risk in a field this size with this profile.

watchPoints.text: Never Mind Me's 683-day absence is the race's single biggest unknown — if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness or is sluggish away, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race opens up dramatically for prominent types.

Reponse Finale ran yesterday (1d LR) and any watch-list alarm should focus here — a horse asked to run back on consecutive days at Dundalk is an extreme fitness question and Gavin Cromwell's explanation will be worth monitoring pre-race.

With 17 runners of which the majority are hold-up types compressed into midfield, a significant bunching or checking incident in the home straight is a realistic risk — horses drawn wide (high stalls) may actually benefit by avoiding the inner traffic.

Movin And Groovin's recent Dundalk win over this trip is form that cannot be ignored, but his true hold-up style being forced forward by field density means he may race uncomfortably — watch whether Nathan Crosse attempts to sit in or is pushed forward early.

Queen Leila and Cause I Like You both won last time out over this course and distance on Standard — their course-specific winning form makes them the two most interesting hold-up types if the pace does materialise to suit a late challenge.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Red God Handicap

runners_data.name: Iron Fist
runners_data.note: Unbeaten on this track last time and clearly the lone confirmed pace-setter here; Shane Foley is adept at controlling from the front, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is racing slightly out of his natural prominent role — he's best treated as the likely leader rather than a banker, and his Goodwood form (3 of last 5 on good) suggests Standard may suit well enough.

runners_data.name: Apercu
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a blinker; Ronan Whelan takes the ride for A. Oliver and the stable is 2/10 in 14 days, but the sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 comparable surface runs is a concern — needs a truly run race to maximise his staying-on finish.
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back shows Apercu has the ability to compete at this level, and returning after 23 days she arrives in decent order; she has run over today's trip and going before, and at 135 lb from stall one, the mare is worth noting despite being winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood (tp) and comes here just 12 days after a run; O'Callaghan stable is 2/14 in the fortnight and Genoah's sim-going figures of 4W5P from 15 runs stands out as the most compelling course-and-distance profile in the field — his natural closing style ideally needs a strong pace to exploit.
runners_data.comment: Genoah drops into this off a sixth last time out, though a second three starts back hints at better, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 135 lb from stall 12 on a rating of 90 makes life tough, but he is at least race-fit on a 12-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old fitted with a visor; ran just three days ago which is an obvious fitness flag, though he clearly handles quick turnarounds — McDonogh keeps the ride and Star Harbour's four placed efforts at 12f on good ground show he handles this sort of trip well from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Star Harbour has been winless in his last six starts, though a pair of runner-up finishes at his best suggest ability, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is the quick three-day turnaround and his tendency to find one or two too good.

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Durkan's yard has sent no runners in the past 14 days (0/6) which is worth noting; Touch The Moon's last win came over 16f on good and the drop back to 10f here is a potential concern, though the 15-day freshener and one placed run on sim-going suggest he can be competitive racing prominently.
runners_data.comment: Finished second three starts back and a winner four starts back, Touch The Moon arrives here fit on a 15-day turnaround, has run over today's trip, and carries 134 lb from stall six; the risk is that his last two runs have yielded an eighth and a fourth.

runners_data.name: Crypto Force
runners_data.note: 112 days off the track is a glaring flag for this hold-up type fitted with a hood (p); the four recent runs on Standard have all been placed (0W4P from 15 sim-going runs) but the layoff and a step back to 10f from open-distance trips makes this a speculative entry rather than a live contender on current form.
runners_data.comment: Crypto Force has experience of today's trip and conditions and, rated 96 against his rivals here, he shapes as a live threat despite carrying 132 lb from stall nine; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with two unplaced efforts most recently.

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse heading a trip shorter than his recent form over 17-18f suggests he prefers; the hood (p) is retained and the one sim-going win from seven tries shows some synthetic-surface aptitude, but Adam Caffrey will need to conjure a strong late run from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Tribal Star showed up well for a second two starts back but has struggled either side of that effort, leaving him winless in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 132 lb from stall 11 makes this no easier.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type whose five recent runs have all produced mid-to-rear finishes on good ground; the sim-going record of 1W1P from 15 runs is modest, and stepping up from 9f trips suggests McAteer is hoping the extra half-mile draws out a performance that flat seven and nine furlong outings have not.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Slieve Binnian arrives 37 days since a seventh and has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, though his recent form offers limited encouragement and, rated 89 by us, he shapes as a midfield player at best from stall seven carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: A genuinely deep hold-up performer whose two recent placed runs at 13f and 12f (both on good) show real ability at this sort of trip; Seamie Heffernan takes over but the REDISTRIBUTED note means Beauparc will race closer than his natural style dictates, which slightly dilutes the chance of a trademark late swooping finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Beauparc at least ran second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, though two further sixths in recent starts suggest consistency remains elusive at 124 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: Fitted with a visor and returning after 46 days off — the longest absence in the field; a natural rear-of-field type pushed into midfield on the map, so Dylan Browne McMonagle faces the challenge of positioning him against his instincts, and the recent form string of 04-983 does not inspire confidence at this stage of preparation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Follow Me faces a stiff task, and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past 14 days does little to inspire confidence, though he does have distance experience and a third last time out to note.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: A blinker-wearing four-year-old who ran well for second on Standard 26 days ago (the sim-going record is 0W1P from just 5 runs, so limited evidence); Wayne Lordan handles him and the redistribution from true hold-up to mapped midfield means he may be inconvenienced if he cannot get back to his preferred closing position in a field this size.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Steel Cut faces a stiff ask here; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but little else in his recent profile invites confidence.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Consistent in terms of placing (2W5P from 15 sim-going runs) but recent form of 408844 shows nothing better than fourth; Ryan rides a horse whose natural closing style is compromised by redistribution into midfield — the step up from 7-8f trips to 10f is a positive query but the handicap mark of OR=78 reflects a horse searching for his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Quatre Bras at least shows some consistency with three fourth-place finishes in that sequence, though the pair of eighths and an unplaced effort are a concern; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 30 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old claiming rider Wesley Joyce (3) takes the mount — the only apprentice in the race; Cala Bonita's last win came over 8f on soft and the step up in trip and switch to Standard turf is untested, but the horse has placed four times in recent outings and tracks the pace in a style that suits a controlled-tempo race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cala Bonita faces a stiff ask despite winning last time out, as her form beyond that has been patchy in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and going, and 16 days on from that victory she arrives reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery riding his own charge (3/30 in 14 days) is a strong angle; the three-year-old has placed in four of his last five including a win at 10f on good and second on Standard, giving him the most relevant recent form of any prominent racer in the field outside the top three in the market.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Nermal faces a stiff ask at his current rating, and a fourth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he did score the start before that and has experience of today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Iron Fist is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of 14, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Standard Dundalk turf over 1m2½f. Star Harbour, Touch The Moon, Slieve Binnian, Cala Bonita, and Nermal will press forward to prominent positions just behind, creating a compact front group but without the pressure that would turn this into a true test of stamina. The hold-up brigade — Apercu, Genoah, Tribal Star, and Crypto Force — will settle in behind, though several horses tagged as natural hold-up types (Steel Cut, Follow Me, Beauparc, Quatre Bras) have been pushed into midfield on the map because the field holds more come-from-behind types than can comfortably occupy the rear; in practice, Iron Fist and Star Harbour are most likely to actually secure the front positions. With a lone, uncontested pace-setter able to control tempo, this race shape decisively favours prominent racers who track the leader comfortably and have the finishing kick to pounce from close range, rather than deep closers who need a true-run affair to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iron Fist Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Iron Fist is left alone to set a measured pace, gifting a cheap lead to himself and those tracking closely.
scenarios.body: Iron Fist rolls along in front at a tempo he dictates, with Star Harbour and Nermal sitting just off his shoulder; when the sprint begins in the final two furlongs, those in the slipstream have first use of their energy and the race is decided between the front two or three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected, allowing the second wave of prominent racers to wear down the front rank late.
scenarios.body: Touch The Moon or Nermal, travelling smoothly just off the pace, pick up the pieces as the front-runner tires in the final furlong on a track where pace figures are Standard throughout the card.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Iron Fist sets a genuinely brisk early tempo that strings the field out and the race develops into a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: Apercu or Genoah, both with strong form profiles on similar ground and distances, close from midfield as the pace collapses in front; Genoah's sim-going record of 4W5P in 15 comparable runs is particularly relevant here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead aggressively, creating an unusually fast early fractions that results in a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up horses — Steel Cut, Follow Me, and Beauparc — who are unlikely to get their natural rear position, find themselves racing much closer than ideal and the race turns into a messy affair where a midfield type sneaks through.

watchPoints.text: Iron Fist holds an uncontested lead — if Shane Foley gets a soft time of it in front with no pressure, the race may be over before the pack can close, making him the key danger if allowed to dictate completely.
Star Harbour ran just three days ago and could be feeling that effort in the closing stages — watch for him to weaken inside the final furlong if the pace has taken its toll before the run-in.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Steel Cut, Follow Me, Beauparc, Quatre Bras) could cause a congestion problem in midfield on a tight Dundalk track, creating scrimmaging and interference in the early-to-middle stages.

Nermal's trainer-rider combination and his Standard-going placed form make him one to monitor in the prominent group — if he travels better than Iron Fist in the straight, his finishing effort could be decisive in a scenario where the leader fades.

Crypto Force's 112-day layoff means he may need this run physically — watch his early-race demeanour and whether Donagh O'Connor sends him forward or holds him up, as either choice risks his chance given both the absence and the natural closing style.

races.name: Friday Night Lights Return Weekly From 18th September Handicap

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has repeatedly faded in the finish at 10f-12f, and five of his last six runs show double-figure finishes; the visor is worn here and Adrian McGuinness sends him out fresh off 9 days, but his form on Standard at Dundalk reads just 6th from 15 attempts with zero wins.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dancing Steve nevertheless catches the eye on a speed figure of 74 that sits well clear of his official mark of 56, and having run over today's distance and going he arrives fit on a nine-day turnaround from stall four carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type returning after 34 days off with Martin Hassett, who has struck at just zero from four over the last fortnight; only one placing from seven runs on Standard going and has faded in three of his last five starts, making this tough.
runners_data.comment: Navajo Point arrives here as the top-rated runner in this field of 17, carrying experience on today's going and drawn in stall one, and his speed rating of 78 makes a compelling case for him to go close; the concern is that he has been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a decent recent placed effort (3rd, 11f, Good) and a win on Standard going; Anthony McCann's yard has found the scorer once from six runners in the past 14 days, and the 29-day freshener could suit a horse who needs to travel positively to be effective.
runners_data.comment: Rising Sky has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 64 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark of 56 implies, giving her a plausible case as a sneaky threat from stall 2; the risk is that she remains winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Anchors Away
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fitted with a tongue-tie, returning 37 days off for M G Quinn who has no runners in the last fortnight; has placed twice in nine Standard-going runs and his best Dundalk effort was a 3rd over 10f, so the trip is not a concern but his propensity to fade is.
runners_data.comment: Anchors Away arrives here 37 days fresh, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour, and our rating of 64 marks him as a lively threat despite being winless in recent starts; the chief concern is a sequence that includes two unplaced efforts heading into this.

runners_data.name: Storm Eric
runners_data.note: The form pick on this surface — 11 from 15 runs on Standard going and five placings in his last five Dundalk appearances over 10f; Adam Grant rides and the 8-day turnaround for Jamie Flynn suggests the horse is in good order, making him the standout hold-up profile for any shape that generates a real gallop.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Storm Eric has finished out of the frame just once in his last six starts yet remains winless in that spell; he has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on just eight days' rest, and a rating of 62 gives him a shade in hand over his mark.

runners_data.name: Tortola
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map slot because the field is overloaded with closers; carries a headgear change (hood) and is 31 days fresh, but his Standard form reads just 5 from 11 with one placing and his style-fit discount (0.93) reflects he will likely race further back than mapped.
runners_data.comment: Tortola showed promise with a second two starts back but has otherwise struggled for consistency in recent starts, and she remains winless in her last five; experience over today's trip and going is a positive, though 139 lb from stall 11 is no easy task.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Blinkers on for A. Oliver, who has sent out two winners from ten in the last fortnight; truly a hold-up type placed into midfield by the race shape rather than his own instinct — his two STA placings (2nd over 12f) show he stays well, but he needs a searching gallop to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Copper Craft does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back offers encouragement, though a seventh before it and an unplaced effort since temper expectations from stall six off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 3-year-old filly in blinkers, arriving 35 days fresh; only one outing on Standard going with zero placings from six runs, and while the De Bromhead stable has fired in four winners from 35 lately, the form string of four finishes outside the frame suggests she needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Retro Gal at least shaped with more promise on her latest outing and has experience of today's distance and going, though a career-high 133 lb from stall five is a stiff ask for a filly rated 56.

runners_data.name: Barretstown
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old with two career wins at Dundalk (both on Standard), but 71 days off the track and trainer Conor O'Dwyer has zero from two in the past fortnight; mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type, and his last win here came over 10f so the trip is fine — it's the layoff and form (0-0-3-7-0-0) that worries.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with only one placed effort — third four starts back — and two unplaced runs since, Barretstown faces a stiff task off 132 lb from stall seven, and 71 days off the track adds further doubt despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare in a tongue-tie who has raced in midfield more by necessity here; M M Rice has no runners in the fortnight and her last 15 STA runs produced zero wins and one placing — she has shown she stays 12f on Standard but the finish-fade flag and relentless placed-outside-frame form make her hard to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn 14 carrying 131 lb, My Vonnie faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 56 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark of 45 implies.

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and key pace-setter, handled by the experienced Seamie Heffernan; W R Crawford sends him out after a 56-day break with two runs over 7f-10f on Standard giving just one placing, and the fade-in-finish flag is a genuine concern if he leads them a proper gallop — but on a Standard surface at Dundalk, the controlled pace may be enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Coul Dore at least showed promise with a second two starts back, though a ninth on his most recent outing is harder to ignore; he has experience over today's trip and going, but 130 lb from stall 16 after a 56-day break makes progress a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Feenagh Moran takes the 10lb claimer's allowance on a horse whose last six runs show nothing but single-figure finishes (best a 6th); mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type, and with zero form on Standard going he is difficult to recommend at any price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Shahada Ace faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 21-day break with conditions at least familiar.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in a tongue-tie with Terry Casey (7lb claim) aboard for Patrick Magee; his best effort was a 2nd over 13f on Good, and his five Standard-going runs produced five placings from zero wins — the longer trip suits his staying profile but he remains a hold-up type pushed into a crowded midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13th of 17 on our figures, Wingit faces a stiff ask from stall 17 carrying 125 lb, though she does bring distance and going experience and a second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Threebiggulps
runners_data.note: J G Coogan's 3-year-old with a hood, 44 days off and only one placing from five Standard-going runs; form reading 0-0-9-9-0 tells a clear story and, as another redistributed hold-up type in a congested rear, the handicapper's mark of 40 reflects his current standing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a string of unplaced and ninth-place efforts, Threebiggulps is hard to fancy from stall 15 on a rating of 40, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns reasonably fresh after 44 days off.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Showing the best recent trajectory in the race — winner over 9f (GOO), placed third over 9f, and 4th over 10f on Standard — Richard Brabazon's 4-year-old has genuine tactical versatility; mapped to midfield rather than his hold-up role by necessity, and with Jack Cleary (5lb claim) he could be the best-handicapped runner if he secures a pitch closer to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Yquem won three starts back but has since posted a third and a fourth, suggesting she's finding life tougher of late; she has run over today's trip and going, and at 136 lb from stall 10 the weight ask is notable for a filly rated just 50 officially.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: H Rogers sends out the 3-year-old in a hood just 14 days after his last run; form of 0-0-6-0 is modest but the 4/10f GOO placing and the yard's 1-from-7 recent strike rate offer a small crumb — he fades in the finish and is a genuine hold-up type without the Standard form to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Chloe's Boy faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround at least suggesting he is fit enough to go.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Consistent performer who has placed twice from two runs over 12f and once over 14f, with a win on Good over 12f for Cian Hughes; mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type but his versatility — shown by finishing 2nd twice over 12f — means he could genuinely slot closer to the pace and would be a major beneficiary of Scenario B.
runners_data.comment: Without Love has shown consistent placed efforts in recent starts, finishing second twice in his last six, but remains winless and a sixth last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 137 lb from stall nine.

races.paceDynamic: Coul Dore is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-horse field and, with no genuine pace pressure from another leader, Seamie Heffernan can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop around Dundalk's flat 1m2½f circuit. Rising Sky and Dancing Steve will push forward from the prominent positions, but neither has the profile to seriously contest the lead, meaning Coul Dore should travel comfortably on the front end without being harried. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up or midfield horses — Storm Eric, Without Love, Copper Craft, Barretstown, Yquem and others all want to come from behind, and on a Standard surface at Dundalk where the pace is likely to be measured rather than searching, those deep hold-up types face a stiffer test than usual. This race shape — a lone leader controlling a moderate gallop with a large cluster of hold-up horses unable to all get clear runs — strongly favours the prominent and pace-pressing profile, as horses that can track Coul Dore just off the pace will be best placed when the sprint home begins. The field contains far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; of the redistributed runners, Without Love and Yquem — both with genuine staying form and tactical versatility — are most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace than their mapped midfield slot suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coul Dore Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore leads comfortably, dictates a measured gallop and the hold-up pack get stuck in traffic turning for home.
scenarios.body: Coul Dore, handled by Heffernan, sets a controlled pace that robs the closers of the strong gallop they need, and the horse's fade-in-finish flag becomes irrelevant if the winning post comes early enough in the sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Presser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore's moderate pace allows a tracking horse to cruise into contention from 2f out and win with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A horse like Storm Eric or Without Love, travelling prominently rather than their natural rear position, times a run off the controlled fractions to pick up the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final half-mile to string the field out and create a clear late-running lane.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer navigates the large field traffic, finds daylight, and picks off the tiring leaders in the final furlong — Storm Eric's excellent Dundalk Standard form fits this best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore sets such a crawl that the field concertinas entering the straight and a sprint finish ensues.
scenarios.body: A wide-draw or prominent horse produces a sharp turn of foot in the mass sprint that negates the slow early pace — Dancing Steve or Navajo Point could benefit from a compressed finish where fitness gaps close.

watchPoints.text: Coul Dore (Heffernan) is the only horse guaranteed a clear lead — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged or whether Rising Sky or Dancing Steve push forward to pressure him in the first half-mile, as that single factor defines the entire race shape.

Storm Eric has the best Standard-going profile in the field (11/15 on the surface, five placings in his last five over this trip at Dundalk) — if he travels smoothly in the early stages and gets a clear passage turning for home, he is the most dangerous hold-up type regardless of scenario.

With nine or more genuine hold-up horses all needing to come from the rear, a severe traffic-jam in the straight is highly probable — watch for horses getting blocked on the inside as the field bunches entering the home turn, particularly Copper Craft and Barretstown drawn into the pack.

Yquem's recent form (1st, 3rd, 4th) makes him the most unexposed improving profile here — watch his early positioning under Jack Cleary; if he manages to track the pace rather than settle deep, his chance is markedly higher than his hold-up tag suggests.

Coul Dore's 56-day layoff combined with his fade-in-finish flag means the critical watch point is how he travels in the final 2f — if he visibly tires before the furlong pole, the race becomes entirely about which hold-up horse gets the clearest late run.
